title: An ocean at fingernail speed
hook: Continents creep at the pace your nails grow. How long does that take to build an ocean?

knows: that the Atlantic separates South America and Africa
doesNotKnow: how much time it takes such a slow speed to make an ocean

misconception: Continents move fast enough to notice, or not at all in human terms; both miss the scale.
objective: The learner can compute that 2.5 cm a year opens 3,000 km in 120 million years, and explain that tiny rates times geological time make oceans.

claims.text: At 2.5 cm a year, widening an ocean by 3,000 km takes 120 million years; each million years adds 25 km.
claims.source: 3,000 km = 3 x 10^8 cm; 3 x 10^8 / 2.5 = 1.2 x 10^8 years. Computed in Demo.tsx (TARGET_MYR, gapKm).

claims.text: Plates move about 2.5 cm a year, the same order as fingernail growth (about 4 cm a year).
claims.source: Fingernails grow about 3 to 3.5 mm a month, about 3.5 to 4 cm a year (dermatology references, e.g. Yaemsiri et al. 2010, J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol, 3.47 mm/month; from memory, not checked online). The lesson's 2.5 cm a year is the same order; the comparison is 'about'. DISPUTED 2026-10-13: The predict question reads 'Plates move about as fast as fingernails grow, 2.5 cm a year', which attributes 2.5 cm a year to fingernails. Yaemsiri et al. 2010 (checked via search): fingernails grow 3.47 mm/month, about 4.2 cm a year, so 2.5 cm is about 40% too low for nails. Fix: 'Plates move about 2.5 cm a year, the same order as fingernail growth (about 4 cm)'. | CLAIM FIX 2026-10-13: Was 'Plates move about as fast as fingernails grow' with the predict question attributing 2.5 cm a year to nails (disputed: nails grow about 3.47 mm/month = 4.2 cm/yr, Yaemsiri et al. 2010). Predict question now says 'Plates move about 2.5 cm a year, the same order as fingernail growth (about 4 cm a year).'

claims.text: Real spreading in the Atlantic varies along the ridge and over time, about 2 to 4 cm a year.
claims.source: Full spreading rates of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge are about 2 to 4 cm a year, slower in the north (USGS 'This Dynamic Earth: Plate Motions'; NASA Earth Observatory; from memory, not checked online).

claims.text: 2.5 cm a year is about 2 metres in a lifetime.
claims.source: 2.5 cm x 80 years = 200 cm. 'Lifetime' taken as about 80 years.

claims.text: The stage is a toy: South America's shapes slide due west at a steady average rate; it is not a plate reconstruction.
claims.source: Demo.tsx rotates the 1:110m South American country shapes about the Earth's axis by (rate x time) / (R cos 10 degrees), so the stated distance is exact along 10 S and smaller toward the south. Labelled 'Toy' on the stage.

recall.question: A rift opens at 5 cm a year. Roughly how long until it is 1,000 km wide?
recall.why: 1,000 km is 100 million cm. At 5 cm a year that is 20 million years: slow speeds times geological time make oceans.
